title: Decoding and Type Coercion Inconsistencies
platform_conditions: Swift runtime semantics (Codable, Any/NSNumber bridging); applies wherever Swift runs, with JSONSerialization bridging behavior defined by the Apple Foundation / swift-corelibs-foundation implementations
security_mechanism: JSONSerialization returns Any dictionaries whose values are NSNumber, and NSNumber bridges to Bool in a way that surprises: 0/1 and true/false are interchangeable through CFBoolean bridging, so an 'isAdmin': 1 numeric field can satisfy a Bool check written against a different shape. 'as?' chains over Any give silent fallbacks per level, so a payload that shifts a field from String to [String] takes a different (often unvalidated) branch instead of failing. try? JSONDecoder().decode(...) collapses every decode error into nil, indistinguishable from 'field absent', so authorization code cannot tell a malformed attacker payload from a missing permission and may default to allow. A lenient custom init(from:) that returns defaults for unparseable values has the same allow-by-default effect, and raw-value enum initialization (Role(rawValue: x) ?? .member) falls back to a benign-looking role on out-of-range input.

source_sink_clues.source: JSON/protobuf request bodies, push and deep-link payloads, and any attacker-chosen field type variations (number vs bool vs array vs null).
source_sink_clues.sink: try? JSONDecoder().decode on authorization-relevant models; 'as?' chains over JSONSerialization Any output; NSNumber-to-Bool/Int bridges compared in security checks; custom init(from:) with default-value fallbacks; enum Role(rawValue:) ?? .default on role fields

tracking_guards: Check decode errors are surfaced and rejected (do/catch with a denial path), not folded into nil-by-default; check decoded models pin field types strictly (no Any, explicit types) and role/state enums decode via throws rather than rawValue fallback; check NSNumber comparisons go through an explicit type test (obj is Bool / obj is Int) before any security comparison.
not_candidate_when: The decoded model only feeds display rendering with no security decision, the payload originates from the app's own backend with a fixed schema verified by tests, or the decode failure path explicitly denies rather than defaulting.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: let user = try? JSONDecoder().decode(User.self, from: data)
synthetic_safe_example: do { let user = try JSONDecoder().decode(User.self, from: data) } catch { ... }
